deep.reconstruction:
Notation (from the tableau on p.38): F(α,β,γ) = F(α,β,γ;x) = Σ (α)_r(β)_r/(r!(γ)_r) x^r is Gauss's hypergeometric series, and F'(α,β,γ) = dF/dx. In the tableau the coefficient of x^{r-1} in F' is rC and the coefficient of x^r is C(r+α)(r+β)/(r+γ) = (r+1)C_{r+1}, which confirms this reading. Each formula on this page expresses a contiguous function, or its derivative, linearly in F and F' with coefficients rational in x. This continues the programme stated on p.38: if the parameter shifts are integers, F(α',β',γ') and F'(α',β',γ') are rational in F and F'.

[17] Differentiate [15], F(α,β+1,γ+1) = -γ/(α-γ) F + γ(1-x)/(β(α-γ)) F'. Then eliminate F'' using the hypergeometric equation (my step; Gauss probably compared coefficients instead). The result is F'(α,β+1,γ+1) = αγ/((α-γ)x) F - γ(γ-αx)/(β(α-γ)x) F'. [16] is the α↔β mirror.

[18] F(α-1,β,γ-1) = (γ-1-βx)/(γ-1) F + x(1-x)/(γ-1) F'. Coefficient check (mine): the RHS coefficient of x^r is [(γ-1+r)C_r - (β+r-1)C_{r-1}]/(γ-1). This equals C_r(γ+r-1)(α-1)/((α+r-1)(γ-1)), which is the LHS coefficient.

[19] is the α↔β mirror of [18].

[20] F'(α-1,β,γ-1) = (α-1)β/(γ-1) F + (α-1)x/(γ-1) F'. It follows from d/dx F(α-1,β,γ-1) = (α-1)β/(γ-1) F(α,β+1,γ) together with F(α,β+1,γ) = F + (x/β)F'. [21] is the mirror.

[22]–[25] and [28] (shifts (±1,±1,0) and (-1,-1,-1)) are left blank on the page.

[26] F(α+1,β+1,γ+1) = γ/(αβ) F', i.e. dF/dx = (αβ/γ)F(α+1,β+1,γ+1).

[27] F'(α+1,β+1,γ+1) = γ/(x-x²) F - γ(γ-(α+β+1)x)/(αβ(x-x²)) F'.

[29] F'(α-1,β-1,γ-1) = (α-1)(β-1)/(γ-1) F.

A marginal note in another (probably editorial) hand says: 'the foregoing was published in Comment. Recent. Soc. Gott. T. II', i.e. the 1812/13 Disquisitiones generales circa seriem infinitam.

[30] Differentiating [26] gives F'(α+1,β+1,γ+1) = γ/(αβ) F''. Equating this with [27] gives the hypergeometric differential equation in Gauss's sign convention: αβF - (γ-(α+β+1)x)F' - (x-x²)F'' = 0. Gauss cites 'Gleichungen 1 und 27'; eq. 1 is presumably the derivative relation [26].

Then let P = F(x) and Q = F(1-x). P satisfies the equation above. For Q, substituting x→1-x sends d/dx → -d/dx, so αβQ - (α+β+1-γ-(α+β+1)x)Q' - (x-x²)Q'' = 0. Thus Q satisfies the same type of equation with γ replaced by α+β+1-γ.

The page ends by singling out the case 2γ = α+β+1. There P and Q satisfy the identical equation. Continued on p.40, this leads to the Wronskian Q P' - P Q' = A(x-x²)^{-γ} (Abel/Liouville style), the evaluation A = 1/π for α=β=1/2, γ=1, and Euler's transformation [32]. The purpose is to study the analytic continuation / second solution at x=1 and the connection between the solutions at 0 and 1.
errors: No mathematical errors found; [17]–[21], [26], [27], [29], [30] and the equation for Q all check.
[30] originally had a '+' before (x-xx)F'' which Gauss struck and corrected to '-'; the corrected sign is right. The same correction appears in the P and Q equations.

The reference 'Gleichungen 1 und 27' is slightly loose. Strictly, [30] needs the derivative of [26] (presumably what eq. 1 states) combined with [27]; it is not circular only if [27] was obtained independently by coefficient comparison, as the p.38 tableau suggests.

results.what: Contiguous relations expressing F and dF/dx at shifted parameters (α,β+1,γ+1), (α-1,β,γ-1), (α,β-1,γ-1), (α+1,β+1,γ+1), (α-1,β-1,γ-1) linearly via F, F'
results.modern_name: Gauss contiguous relations / derivative (shift) formulas for 2F1

results.what: Hypergeometric differential equation x(1-x)F'' + (γ-(α+β+1)x)F' - αβF = 0 derived from contiguous relations
results.usually_credited_to: Euler (1769/1778); Gauss (Nachlass part 2 of the 1812 memoir, Werke III); Kummer 1836

results.what: F(α,β,γ;1-x) satisfies the hypergeometric equation with γ replaced by α+β+1-γ; in the case 2γ=α+β+1 both F(x) and F(1-x) solve the same equation
results.modern_name: Solutions at x=1 of the hypergeometric equation (Kummer's solutions), symmetric case
results.usually_credited_to: Kummer 1836; Gauss Nachlass (Werke III, 'Determinatio seriei nostrae per aequationem differentialem')

deep.surprise_reason: This is a German draft of material known from Gauss's 1812 hypergeometric memoir and its posthumously published second part (Werke III). The contiguous/derivative relations and the differential equation are well known as Gauss's. The x→1-x observation is likewise in the published Nachlass.

checkable.sympy: a,b,c,x=symbols('a b c x'); F=lambda A,B,C: hyper([A,B],[C],x); simplify(hyperexpand(diff(F(a,b+1,c+1),x) - (a*c/((a-c)*x)*F(a,b,c) - c*(c-a*x)/(b*(a-c)*x)*diff(F(a,b,c),x))).subs({a:Rational(1,3),b:Rational(1,5),c:Rational(7,4)}))

[30] hypergeometric ODE in Gauss's sign convention (series vanishes)
If y solves the equation, Q(x)=y(1-x) solves a*b*Q-(a+b+1-c-(a+b+1)x)Q'-(x-x²)Q''=0

transcription_corrections: [18]: the numerator is γ-1-βx; Gauss overwrote a digit in 'γ-1'.
[20]: the first coefficient's numerator and denominator are overwritten in the manuscript; the intended reading (α-1)β/(γ-1) is mathematically confirmed.
[26]: the right side has a gap before γ/(αβ)F'(α,β,γ), with no F term; the transcription is correct.
[30] and the P, Q equations: a '+' was struck and replaced by '-' before (x-xx)F''. The correct reading is '- (x-xx)F''', not '[-+-]'.
In the P equation a stray '1' precedes dP ('1dP/dx'); it should read dP/dx.
Marginal note in a different hand: 'Das bisherige bekannt gemacht Comment. Recent. Soc. Gott. T. II.'
